UN Loss and Damage Fund Earmarks $20 Million for Nepal Following August Disasters

28 Oct 2026, 09:06 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Climate Desk · Source: www.thehindu.com

Historic Allocation for Nepal

The United Nations climate convention's Loss and Damage Fund has provisionally set aside $21.6 million for Nepal to address recovery from the severe Bhotekoshi river system floods in August. The decision, reached during an extraordinary meeting of the Fund's Board on Thursday, October 22, 2026, marks the first time the mechanism has earmarked specific financial support for an individual country to remedy climate-induced damages.

The allocation includes approximately $20 million for reconstruction alongside $1.6 million designated as oversight fees. These fees cover costs paid to implementing organizations—such as multilateral banks, national institutions, and UN agencies—to supervise project execution.

Background and Disaster Context

On August 26, 2026, a climate-induced ice-and-rock avalanche triggered a catastrophic debris flow and flooding along the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli-Narayani river system in Nepal. In response, Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Agriculture, Forests and Environment Minister Gita Chaudhary submitted a formal appeal to the Fund’s co-chairs on August 31, urging a rapid and direct response.

Nepal, classified as a least developed country with negligible contributions to global greenhouse gas emissions, faces heavy economic tolls from warming regional temperatures. Government assessments place initial recovery and reconstruction needs at a minimum of $4.71 billion, with total economic losses estimated around $5 billion. Additionally, the nation has announced plans to study and drain four vulnerable glacial lakes over the coming years to mitigate future disaster risks.

Global Financial Realities and Constraints

Established at COP27 in 2022 with operational frameworks finalized at COP28, the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage is designed to assist vulnerable developing nations with both economic and non-economic losses. However, the $20 million allocation represents less than 0.5% of Nepal's self-assessed recovery costs.

The global mechanism faces significant financial strain. While total donor pledges exceed $820 million—with $342 million promised for the start-up phase—the Fund has received 176 requests from 119 countries totaling approximately $2.8 billion. Actual disbursements depend heavily on donors fulfilling their pledges in a timely manner.

Practical Implications and Verification

  • Confirmed Facts: The UN Loss and Damage Fund Board provisionally earmarked $21.6 million (including $20 million for reconstruction and $1.6 million in oversight fees) for Nepal on October 22, 2026, following the August 26 avalanche and flood event.
  • Uncertainties: The exact timeline for cash disbursement remains tied to donor pledge fulfillment and the completion of formal project proposals. The total extent of economic and non-economic losses is still being evaluated.
  • Reader Verification: Readers can review the original reporting and official announcements through [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/energy-and-environment/un-climate-damages-fund-earmarks-20-million-to-nepal-for-august-disaster/article71612344.ece).
